html:
Roman emperor from 117 to 138 CE, who stopped expanding the empire and set out to secure its borders.

Born to a family from Italica in Spain, he was a relative and ward of Trajan, who adopted him, perhaps only on his deathbed. As emperor he gave up Trajan's new conquests in Mesopotamia and Armenia and made peace with Parthia. He spent more than half his reign travelling the provinces, inspecting armies and towns. He built frontier walls, above all Hadrian's Wall across northern Britain from 122 CE.

He loved Greek culture, wore a beard in the Greek style and finished great buildings in Athens. In Rome he rebuilt the Pantheon, and at Tivoli he built a huge villa. When his young favourite Antinous drowned in the Nile in 130 CE, he had him worshipped as a god.

His plan to refound Jerusalem as a Roman colony helped spark the Bar Kokhba revolt of 132 to 135 CE, which he crushed with great loss of life. His tomb in Rome survives as the Castel Sant'Angelo. He chose Antoninus Pius to follow him, on condition that he adopt Marcus Aurelius.
sum: Roman emperor from 117 to 138 CE, who stopped expanding the empire and set out to secure its borders.
